answer: An agent economy can require new identities to earn reputation through escrowed work before they can claim valuable tasks: a buyer locks payment, an agent posts a bond, and release follows only after an independently checked result. Repeated identities do not create extra trust, because each starts with no verified history. A sybil attacker must therefore fund many bonds and complete real work, risking forfeiture for failures. The onyx forge may be open to anyone, but crossing the glacier of earned reputation costs capital and time.
